title: Value of Photon Counting Computer Tomography for Breast Diagnosis
summary: Photon counting computed tomography (PC-CT) is a new CT technology for routine clinical use that enables image data sets with higher spatial resolution and lower radiation dose. Especially in breast imaging, high spatial resolution is important, which could not be achieved by previous CT techniques and currently can only be achieved by mammography, tomosynthesis, and dedicated breast CT systems. In contrast to the aforementioned methods, PC-CT offers the additional advantage of contrast agent application and supplementary spectral analysis. All in all, this provides us with a new procedure that can be expected to be equivalent to mammography/tomosynthesis and possibly better in some respects, particularly with regard to masses in the breast. In every CT of the thorax, which is also performed in patients with breast carcinoma as part of staging and often medically indicated in other diseases with contrast medium, both breasts are completely imaged, an additional examination with additional radiation application is not necessary. Furthermore, in the case of indicated CT examinations, PC-CT seems to offer a presumably equivalent, yet implicit, cheaper and faster alternative to breast MRI without renewed contrast agent application. Therefore, we aim to assess the diagnostic value of PC-CT for the evaluation of breast masses compared with mammography/tomosynthesis and MRI.

interventions.name: Patients with confirmed breast carcinoma and current mammography/tomosynthesis or clinical indication for mammography/tomosynthesis and clinical indication for CT thorax with contrast. In addition, an MRI of the mamma is performed.

Patients without breast carcinoma with current mammography/tomosynthesis or clinical indication for mammography/tomosynthesis and clinical indication for CT thorax with contrast due to other conditions.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Group A: Patients with confirmed breast carcinoma and current mammography/tomosynthesis or clinical indication for mammography/tomosynthesis and clinical indication for CT thorax with contrast medium
- Group B: Patients without breast carcinoma with current mammography/tomosynthesis or clinical indication for mammography/tomosynthesis and clinical indication for CT thorax with contrast medium due to other diseases.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of recent mammography (not available, no current clinical indication or not feasible)
- Contraindication to contrast medium used
- Prone position not possible for health reasons (necessary for CT and, in the case of group A, for MRI examination)
- Pregnancy or lactation
